stance_basis: letter calling ORVs destructive and demanding severe restrictions and prohibition in wildlife refuges
summary: William Denneen, writing from Allan Hancock College, submitted a letter opposing permissive ORV use on public lands, citing personal observation of destructive impacts including habitat damage, wildlife disturbance from noise, vegetation destruction, and littering. He called for ORVs to be severely restricted and prohibited in wildlife refuges. No agency response to his comment appears in the document window.
complaint_summary: Denneen argues from personal observation that ORVs are destructive to natural habitat—disturbing wildlife with noise, tearing up vegetation, and generating litter—and calls for severe restrictions and prohibition of ORVs in wildlife refuges.

statement.text:
I wish to add my observations to your consideration of offroad-vehicle plans on public lands. We have a considerable number of such vehicles in our area and I have owned one for 12 years.
My observation has been that ORV's have been very destructive to the natural habitat in all areas where they are permitted. The noise disturbs wildlife and people, the tires tear up vegetation and the drivers often leave prodigious quantities of litter. ORV's should be severely restricted and prohibited in wildlife refuges.
Sincerely yours,
Villiam Denneen
